title: Twenty First Word First Station Fifth Warning Rejecting Worldly Busyness As An Excuse

questions.question: What problem is being talked about at the start of this passage?
questions.answer: Being lazy or careless about worship, especially the required prayers.

questions.question: What wrong idea is challenged when the passage asks whether a person was made only for this world?
questions.answer: The wrong idea is that life is only for worldly work and worldly goals.

questions.question: How are humans compared with animals in this passage?
questions.answer: Humans have greater abilities, but they are not meant to live only for food and daily needs like animals.

questions.question: Why is the example of the sparrow used?
questions.answer: It shows that even a small bird can manage worldly needs, so a human’s main job must be higher than just earning a living.

questions.question: According to the passage, what mistake do people make with many so-called worldly occupations?
questions.answer: They get busy with matters that are small, unnecessary, or not really their responsibility.

questions.question: What do the examples about Saturn and the number of chickens in America teach?
questions.answer: They teach that people can waste precious time on useless facts while ignoring what matters most.

questions.question: In the example about the worker, what is the foolish excuse for refusing the ten-minute job?
questions.answer: The excuse is being afraid of losing a tiny amount of pay while missing a far greater gain.

questions.question: What lesson does that worker example teach about prayer?
questions.answer: Missing prayer for a small worldly reason is foolish because prayer brings much greater benefit.

questions.question: What does the orchard stand for in the comparison?
questions.answer: It stands for a person’s work in this world to earn a living.

questions.question: If a person leaves the required prayers, what happens to the results of his work?
questions.answer: His work stays limited to a small, worldly benefit that does not bring lasting gain.

questions.question: When should a person do the prayers according to this passage?
questions.answer: During times of rest, when the spirit can settle and the heart can breathe.

questions.question: What are the two “mines” or treasures found through prayer?
questions.answer: One helps bring blessing into worldly livelihood, and the other brings provision for the hereafter.

questions.question: What is the main message of this passage about worship and daily life?
questions.answer: A person should not let worldly busyness stop him from praying, because prayer brings great benefits in both worlds.

questions.question: Why does the passage ask whether a person was created only for this world?
questions.answer: To remind the reader that human life has a higher purpose than only worldly success.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the true duty of a human being?
questions.answer: A human being should seek an everlasting life with meaning, not live only for physical needs.

questions.question: What is one sign that people may be too attached to worldly matters?
questions.answer: They spend too much time on small or useless topics and neglect what is most important.

questions.question: Why are examples of unusual facts given in the passage?
questions.answer: To show how people can act as if collecting random information is more important than preparing for the hereafter.

questions.question: In the worker example, what is being compared to the small wage loss?
questions.answer: The tiny worldly cost of taking time for prayer.

questions.question: In that same example, what do the precious jewels stand for?
questions.answer: They stand for the much greater reward and benefit found in prayer.

questions.question: Why is the excuse of the worker called foolish?
questions.answer: Because he rejects a huge gain in order to avoid a very small loss.

questions.question: How does this comparison help someone who says earning money keeps him from praying?
questions.answer: It shows that prayer does not truly ruin livelihood; instead, leaving prayer causes a much bigger loss.

questions.question: What does the passage say happens if someone gives up the required prayers while working for livelihood?
questions.answer: His work remains only a small worldly gain without deeper fruit.

questions.question: How can prayer fit into a busy life according to the passage?
questions.answer: It can be done during breaks and moments of rest.

questions.question: What effect do the prayers have on the spirit and heart in this passage?
questions.answer: They refresh the spirit and give relief to the heart.

questions.question: What are the two major gains described after mentioning prayer during rest times?
questions.answer: Better blessing in worldly work and provision for the life to come.

questions.question: What is the first gain connected to gardening work?
questions.answer: Sharing in the worship of the plants and trees that grow.

questions.question: What role does intention play in the first gain?
questions.answer: Good intention is the key that opens that reward.

questions.question: What is the second gain connected to the produce of the garden?
questions.answer: Whatever is eaten from it can count as charity from the worker.

questions.question: What makes that second reward possible?
questions.answer: Working for Allah, following what is lawful, and seeing the goods as belonging to Allah.

questions.question: Who is being addressed in this passage?
questions.answer: The soul that is too attached to worldly life.

questions.question: What excuse for weak worship is examined first?
questions.answer: The excuse of being too busy with worldly work and earning a living.

questions.question: What question helps challenge this excuse?
questions.answer: Whether a person was made only for this world.

questions.question: What higher goal is given for human beings?
questions.answer: To work for a lasting and real life beyond this world.

questions.question: Why does the passage compare humans and animals?
questions.answer: To show that humans should live by a higher purpose than animals do.

questions.question: What does the sparrow example show about earning a living?
questions.answer: Even a tiny bird can manage its needs, so earning is not the whole purpose of being human.

questions.question: What criticism is made of many worldly occupations?
questions.answer: Many are minor matters that people involve themselves in without real need.

questions.question: What is wrong with spending much time on strange facts and trivia?
questions.answer: It wastes valuable time that should be used for more important duties.

questions.question: What kind of matters does the speaker answer after someone says his work keeps him from prayer?
questions.answer: The speaker answers the claim that livelihood is an essential reason for neglecting prayer.

questions.question: In the digging example, what choice is the worker offered?
questions.answer: A short task that would bring something far more valuable than his small lost pay.

questions.question: Why would refusing that offer be unwise?
questions.answer: Because it would trade a huge reward for a tiny gain.

questions.question: How does that story connect to prayer?
questions.answer: Prayer may take a little time, but it brings much greater profit than the small worldly time it uses.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by calling the place of work an orchard?
questions.answer: It uses the orchard as an image for a person’s daily work and earning.

questions.question: If prayers are abandoned, how are the fruits of one’s effort described?
questions.answer: They are described as limited to a weak and low worldly return.

questions.question: What two parts of a person are refreshed by prayer in rest times?
questions.answer: The spirit and the heart.

questions.question: What are the “two mines” meant to show?
questions.answer: They show that prayer opens hidden treasures of reward.

questions.question: What is the first mine about?
questions.answer: Sharing in the worship of the growing plants and trees.

questions.question: Why is intention so important in the first mine?
questions.answer: Because sincere intention connects a person to the reward.

questions.question: What is the second mine about?
questions.answer: The produce becoming like charity when others benefit from it.

questions.question: Does the second mine only apply when good people eat the produce?
questions.answer: No, it can still count even if animals, flies, buyers, or thieves take from it.

questions.question: What must the worker remember about ownership for the second mine?
questions.answer: He must know the goods belong to Allah and he is only handing them out.

questions.question: How might this lack of purpose affect him later in life?
questions.answer: He may become lazy and no longer care about his work.

questions.question: What does the better worker hope to send ahead to his grave?
questions.answer: More light and more provision for the next life.

questions.question: What kind of soul is warned in this passage?
questions.answer: A soul that loves worldly life too much.

questions.question: What behavior shows this unhealthy love of the world?
questions.answer: Neglecting worship because of worldly busyness.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the idea that all of a person’s time should go to worldly matters?
questions.answer: It says that idea is wrong because humans were not made only for this world.

questions.question: What makes humans higher than animals in this discussion?
questions.answer: Humans have greater abilities and a higher purpose.

questions.question: What should humans seek instead of living only like animals?
questions.answer: They should seek a true and lasting life.

questions.question: What does the passage say about many activities people call important worldly work?
questions.answer: Many are actually small and unnecessary matters.

questions.question: Why is being busy with useless information a problem?
questions.answer: Because it takes away time from what is truly needed.

questions.question: What excuse is answered in the next part of the passage?
questions.answer: The excuse that necessary work and earning money leave no time for prayer.

questions.question: In the example of the worker, how long is the extra task?
questions.answer: Ten minutes.

questions.question: What does the worker lose if he accepts the task?
questions.answer: Only a small part of his daily pay.

questions.question: What would he gain from those ten minutes?
questions.answer: Something far more valuable than what he lost.

questions.question: What is the lesson of that comparison?
questions.answer: Giving a little time to prayer is a small cost for a huge gain.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the result of work without prayer?
questions.answer: It becomes only a narrow worldly earning with little real fruit.

questions.question: What is special about using break time for prayer?
questions.answer: Prayer during breaks both rests the soul and brings greater benefit.

questions.question: What are the two kinds of provision mentioned after that?
questions.answer: Provision for worldly life and provision for the hereafter.

questions.question: What is the first hidden treasure a worker may gain?
questions.answer: Reward connected to the worship of the living things he helps grow.

questions.question: What condition is placed on getting that first reward?
questions.answer: The person must have a proper intention.

questions.question: What is the second hidden treasure?
questions.answer: The crops or produce can count as charity when others benefit from them.

questions.question: Why is this second treasure generous and wide-reaching?
questions.answer: Because many different creatures may benefit, and reward can still come from that.

questions.question: What must a worker remember if he wants that reward?
questions.answer: He must work in Allah’s name and within lawful limits.

questions.question: What view of himself should he have?
questions.answer: He should see himself as a servant distributing what belongs to Allah.

questions.question: What does the better person say through his actions?
questions.answer: He says he will increase both worship and lawful work for the next life.

questions.question: What should a person understand about yesterday and tomorrow?
questions.answer: Yesterday is gone and tomorrow is uncertain.

questions.question: What is the “true life” a person definitely has?
questions.answer: The present day.

questions.question: What is one wise use of an hour from today?
questions.answer: To use it for prayer and worship.

questions.question: Why is a mosque or prayer rug compared to a place of savings?
questions.answer: Because worship there stores reward for the future.

questions.question: What is each day compared to besides savings?
questions.answer: A doorway into a new world.

questions.question: What makes that daily world dark?
questions.answer: Failing to perform the prayers.

questions.question: What decides the color and condition of that daily world?
questions.answer: The condition of the person’s inner life and actions.

questions.question: How can a person change his own world?
questions.answer: By his heart, thinking, actions, and desires.

questions.question: What can prayer make the world become?
questions.answer: A world full of light and meaning.

questions.question: What does prayer help a person notice in events around him?
questions.answer: That they happen with wisdom and order, not just confusion.

questions.question: Why are ordinary prayers still important?
questions.answer: Because they still contain a share of the same light as greater prayers.

questions.question: What varies among different people’s prayers?
questions.answer: Their levels and how fully their light appears.

questions.question: What is the central warning in this passage?
questions.answer: Do not let worldly life make you careless about the required prayers.

questions.question: What two possible reasons for neglecting worship are mentioned at the start?
questions.answer: Being busy with many worldly tasks and claiming there is no time because of earning a living.

questions.question: What important question is asked to challenge those excuses?
questions.answer: Whether a person was created only for this world.

questions.question: What does the passage say is not a human being’s main duty?
questions.answer: Living only to work for material needs like an animal.

questions.question: What does it say is closer to a human being’s real duty?
questions.answer: Seeking a true life that lasts forever.

questions.question: How does the passage show that many worldly concerns are exaggerated?
questions.answer: It says many are minor things that people interfere in without need.

questions.question: What is the danger of filling life with unimportant knowledge?
questions.answer: A person neglects the really necessary things.

questions.question: Why are examples of faraway facts used?
questions.answer: To show how people waste time on matters that do not help their real purpose.

questions.question: What answer is given when someone says he is kept from prayer by necessary work?
questions.answer: The answer is a comparison that shows how foolish that excuse is.

questions.question: In the comparison, what is the worker afraid of losing?
questions.answer: A small amount of his daily earnings.

questions.question: What does he fail to appreciate?
questions.answer: A much greater treasure that could be gained in very little time.

questions.question: What does this teach about time spent in prayer?
questions.answer: A little time in prayer is not a real loss but a path to much greater profit.

questions.question: What does the orchard represent in this part of the passage?
questions.answer: A person’s workplace and effort to make a living.

questions.question: What happens if someone works but leaves the required prayers?
questions.answer: The result stays limited to small and low worldly earnings.

questions.question: What good use of free moments is recommended?
questions.answer: Spending them on prayer.

questions.question: What personal benefit of prayer is mentioned right away?
questions.answer: It gives rest to the spirit and relief to the heart.

questions.question: What larger result comes from this besides inner peace?
questions.answer: It opens two great sources of benefit.

questions.question: What is the first source of benefit?
questions.answer: Reward from the worship of the plants and trees one grows.

questions.question: What must a person have to receive that reward?
questions.answer: A sound intention.

questions.question: What is the second source of benefit?
questions.answer: The harvest becomes like charity when creatures eat from it.

questions.question: What wide range of creatures is included in this reward?
questions.answer: Human beings, animals, insects, customers, and even thieves.

questions.question: What three conditions are tied to this second reward?
questions.answer: Working for Allah, staying within what He allows, and seeing oneself as handling His property.

questions.question: What great loss comes from abandoning prayer according to the passage?
questions.answer: Losing valuable spiritual riches and the rewards that would strengthen a person.

questions.question: What emotional result follows this loss?
questions.answer: The person loses enthusiasm and strong morale.

questions.question: How may this affect him in old age?
questions.answer: He may become bored with his work and fall into laziness.

questions.question: What outlook does such a person have toward worldly labor?
questions.answer: He sees no lasting meaning in it.

questions.question: How does the better servant think differently?
questions.answer: He joins worship and lawful work so he can prepare for the grave and the hereafter.

questions.question: What immediate effect do the five daily prayers have on that world?
questions.answer: They brighten it by turning the person toward Allah.

questions.question: What does the lamp image teach about prayer?
questions.answer: Prayer lights up life and makes hidden meaning easier to see.

questions.question: What should a regular person believe about his own prayer?
questions.answer: That it still carries real light and truth, even if it is not as strong as the prayer of great saints.

questions.question: What kind of person is this warning especially speaking to?
questions.answer: A person whose heart is overly attached to worldly matters.

questions.question: What sign of that attachment is mentioned first?
questions.answer: Carelessness in worship and in the required prayers.

questions.question: What basic life question does the passage raise?
questions.answer: Whether human beings were created only for worldly life.

questions.question: What answer does the passage guide us to?
questions.answer: No; humans were made for a higher and lasting purpose.

questions.question: In what way are humans said to be above animals?
questions.answer: In their abilities and higher calling.

questions.question: In what way are humans not meant to compete with animals?
questions.answer: In making material survival their main concern.

questions.question: Why is the example of a sparrow meaningful?
questions.answer: It reminds us that even small creatures get their needs, so human life must be about more than that.

questions.question: What does the passage say about many things people call “worldly occupations”?
questions.answer: Many are unimportant matters that people take on without real need.

questions.question: What is one result of chasing such matters?
questions.answer: Essential duties get neglected.

questions.question: What claim does the passage answer next?
questions.answer: The claim that earning a living leaves no room for prayer.

questions.question: In the story of the paid worker, what makes the refusal unreasonable?
questions.answer: The worker rejects a huge reward because of a very small deduction.

questions.question: What does that say about skipping prayer for worldly work?
questions.answer: It is a poor excuse because the gain from prayer is far greater.

questions.question: What image is used for a person’s work life?
questions.answer: An orchard.

questions.question: If prayer is left out, how valuable are the fruits of that work?
questions.answer: They remain only worldly and of little lasting worth.

questions.question: Why is doing prayer during rest times wise?
questions.answer: Because it brings peace inside while also bringing lasting benefit.

questions.question: What two broad kinds of livelihood are mentioned?
questions.answer: Worldly livelihood and the livelihood of the hereafter.

questions.question: What is the first “mine” or treasure?
questions.answer: A share in the worship of the plants and trees a person grows.

questions.question: What opens that first treasure?
questions.answer: A sincere intention.

questions.question: What is the second treasure?
questions.answer: The produce counting like charity when creatures benefit from it.

questions.question: Does the second treasure depend only on honorable people benefiting?
questions.answer: No, even if lowly creatures or thieves take from it, reward can still come.

questions.question: What view must a person have of his work for this reward to count?
questions.answer: He must do it for Allah and as a caretaker of what belongs to Allah.

questions.question: What does the person lose by abandoning the prayers?
questions.answer: Great wealth of reward and the encouragement that comes with it.

questions.question: What kind of inner collapse may follow?
questions.answer: Weak spirit, poor morale, and laziness.

questions.question: What may such a person say when older and tired?
questions.answer: That there is no point in the struggle since he is leaving the world anyway.

questions.question: What does the more faithful worker aim for instead?
questions.answer: More worship, more lawful effort, and more provision for the next life.
